svg.title: A claims-only install of the Buddy System: clone, run the install script, paste the hook wiring into the Claude Code settings file, then buddy init in another project, the digest a new session gets there, its first claim and what the ledger holds about it
svg.desc: Real output captured 2026-10-25 against a throwaway HOME (the install script's own knobs point every write at it; the clone came from a local mirror of main spelled as the GitHub URL, and the Go build cache was warm). The throwaway HOME's path is written ~; long lines are soft-wrapped at 58 columns and trimmed with an ellipsis; no words were changed. The session's SessionStart hook was run by hand with the payload Claude Code sends. Lines starting with # are narration. Loops every 22 s; under prefers-reduced-motion the final frame is shown still.
svg.text: turn it on in a project — the same terminal

g.text: wired; README "Hook wiring" has the lines
install: handoff: BUDDY_HANDOFF_AT not set in
# the README's hook-wiring block, saved by hand: the
# … 13 more lines: the README's block, verbatim
install: hooks: all six wired in ~/.claude/settings.json
language server: go (2 files) — NOT CONFIGURED: gopls-lsp
# a new Claude Code session here: SessionStart → buddy
hello puts this in its context
BUDDY: `buddy --help` lists every verb. Easy to miss:
$ buddy claim api-limits --desc "rate limits on the
# … 8 lines elided (DIRTY PATHS, BASE, INBOX, ADAPTER,
EXIT 1 claim(s) held; no wait declared; no shell
found running under it — ending now would leave the
